articles.title: Hip Decompression Augmented With Bone Marrow Aspirate Concentrate and Platelet-Rich Plasma for Corticosteroid-Induced Osteonecrosis of the Femoral Head: A Minimum 10-Year Follow-Up.
articles.authors: Restrepo DJ, Smith JH, Guarin Perez SF, Houdek MT, Wyles CC, Sierra RJ
articles.study_type: Prospective cohort study with minimum 10-year follow-up
articles.population: Patients with pre-collapse corticosteroid-induced osteonecrosis of the femoral head
articles.outcomes: Survivorship free from hip replacement and femoral head collapse; Harris Hip Score for functional outcomes; risk factors for failure
articles.take_home: Hip decompression with bone marrow and platelet-rich plasma preserved the hip joint in 62% of patients over 10 years, though success was much lower (40%) in those with larger lesions. Patients whose hips were preserved showed significant improvement in pain and function.

articles.title: Liposomal Bupivacaine in Periarticular Injection Cocktails for Pain Management After Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
articles.authors: Ng MK, Mastrokostas LE, Mastrokostas PG, Mont MA
articles.study_type: Systematic review of randomized controlled trials
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Postoperative pain control, opioid consumption, functional recovery, patient satisfaction, adverse events
articles.take_home: Liposomal bupivacaine injected around the knee during surgery improved pain relief in the first 24 hours after total knee replacement in most studies and reduced opioid use without causing harm. It appears to be a safe option to help with pain management as part of a broader pain control strategy.

articles.title: Keloidosis is Associated with an Increased Risk for Developing Arthrofibrosis After Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Garcia D, Thota P, Dogiparthi A, Suresh K, Siegel N, Rao S, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national electronic health records database with propensity matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing total knee arthroplasty, with a comparison group matched on age, sex, race, ethnicity, comorbidities, and other factors
articles.sample_size: 1,205 patients in each cohort (2,410 total after matching)
articles.outcomes: Arthrofibrosis and revision total knee arthroplasty within one and two years after surgery
articles.take_home: Patients with a history of keloids had about twice the risk of developing arthrofibrosis (stiffness) after knee replacement within one and two years compared to those without keloids. The findings suggest that a tendency to form keloids may increase the risk of problematic scarring inside the knee joint after surgery.

articles.title: Histological analysis of quadriceps tendon collagen composition across physical maturity levels and anatomical layers.
articles.authors: Mizuno Y, Takata Y, Yoshioka K, Takemoto N, Nishimura M, Fujita K, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction or osteochondral autograft harvesting
articles.outcomes: Type I and type III collagen composition in quadriceps tendon samples across three anatomical layers and three maturity groups
articles.take_home: The study found no significant differences in collagen composition of the quadriceps tendon between different age groups or between different layers of the tendon. This suggests that tendon structure remains relatively consistent regardless of physical maturity or anatomical location within the tendon.

articles.title: A standardized 3D modeling method to evaluate measurement accuracy of imageless computer-assisted total knee arthroplasty systems.
articles.authors: Luo TD, Braun SB, Howard JL, McIsaac KA, Lanting BA
articles.population: Computer-assisted total knee arthroplasty systems (two imageless navigation systems)
articles.outcomes: Measurement accuracy, alignment accuracy, and cut surface uniformity of bone resections
articles.take_home: Both navigation systems tested performed well overall, with cut surfaces nearly all within 1 mm of target, though measurements in one plane direction showed more variability. This study developed a standardised method to fairly compare different knee replacement navigation systems without being affected by surgeon differences.

articles.title: Femoral malrotation and patellofemoral osteoarthritis: cadaveric study.
articles.authors: Alhamoud BA, Alrabai HM, Alyahya KI, Alrashidi Y
articles.population: Cadaveric specimens
articles.outcomes: Association between femoral version angle (low, normal, high) and distribution of patellofemoral osteoarthritis (medial facet, lateral facet, or both)
articles.take_home: The study found that abnormal femoral rotation is associated with specific patterns of knee cartilage wear: inward rotation tends to affect the inner knee compartment whilst outward rotation affects the outer compartment. However, the researchers note these are anatomical associations only and further research in living patients is needed to understand whether this actually causes problems.

articles.title: Non-medical surgical delay increases one-year mortality following hip fracture.
articles.authors: Busby C, Nightingale J, Deacon C, Deakin D, Valdes A, Ollivere BJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 60 years and over admitted with fragility hip fracture
articles.outcomes: One-year all-cause mortality and length of hospital stay
articles.take_home: Hip fracture patients whose surgery was delayed more than 36 hours due to lack of surgical capacity had a 20% higher risk of dying within one year compared to those operated on sooner. The longer the delay, the greater the risk.

articles.title: Autologous impaction bone grafting of a cemented acetabular component in primary total hip arthroplasty in young patients: a randomized controlled trial.
articles.authors: de Boer DR, Pasman P, Munnik-Hagewoud R, Steinweg MJQ, Edens MA, van Driel PBAA, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 18 to 59 years undergoing primary total hip replacement without acetabular bone defects
articles.outcomes: Hip function and activities of daily living at one year, patient-reported outcome measures, surgical time, blood loss, complications, revision rates, and radiological assessment of component positioning and bone-cement interface
articles.take_home: Adding bone graft during hip replacement in younger patients does not improve short-term function compared to standard surgery, but it does reduce gaps around the cup on X-rays and may help the hip position stay better long-term. The grafting procedure takes about 7.5 minutes longer and causes slightly more blood loss.

articles.title: Cost-effectiveness of screening for developmental dysplasia of the hip in children born in England and Wales.
articles.authors: Plumpton CO, Perry DC
articles.study_type: Health economic evaluation using decision-analytic modelling
articles.population: Children born in England and Wales
articles.outcomes: Cost-effectiveness of six DDH screening programmes measured by incremental net monetary benefit and quality-adjusted life-years
articles.take_home: Current screening practice in the UK, which involves clinical examination with ultrasound for babies with abnormal findings or risk factors, is the most cost-effective approach. Universal ultrasound screening finds more cases but costs significantly more, making it less economical for the NHS.

articles.title: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists are associated with improved 90-day outcomes after total hip and knee arthroplasty : a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Rudran B, Little CDJ, Palmer AJR, Judge A, Carli A, Price AJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip or knee replacement, many with type 2 diabetes or obesity
articles.sample_size: 96,356 patients across 10 studies (30,350 hip replacements and 66,606 knee replacements)
articles.outcomes: 90-day surgical complications (infection, wound problems, fracture, nerve injury), medical complications, readmission rates, revision surgery rates, and healthcare costs
articles.take_home: Patients taking GLP-1 receptor agonist medications had fewer complications and hospital readmissions within 90 days of hip or knee replacement surgery compared to those not taking these drugs. The benefit was stronger for hip replacements than knee replacements.

articles.title: Periprosthetic joint infection : lessons from the INFORM research programme.
articles.authors: Moore AJ, Beswick AD, Whitehouse MR, Blom AW
articles.study_type: Research programme review and guideline development
articles.population: Patients with periprosthetic joint infection following arthroplasty, with emphasis on hip and knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Risk factors for infection, impact of infection, diagnostic methods, treatment approaches, and evidence-based guidelines for managing periprosthetic joint infection
articles.take_home: The INFORM research programme has comprehensively studied periprosthetic joint infection after joint replacement and developed evidence-based guidelines to help guide clinical decision-making on diagnosis and treatment of this serious complication.

articles.title: Use of neurolytic nerve blocks and mortality in nonoperative management of hip fracture patients : a nationwide population study in the Netherlands.
articles.authors: van Bremen HE, Lommerse MI, Hegeman JH, Schuijt HJ, Kallewaard JW, Wijnen HH, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 70 years and older with hip fractures treated nonoperatively in the Netherlands
articles.outcomes: Mortality at 7 days, 30 days, 3 months, and 6 months
articles.take_home: Patients who received neurolytic nerve blocks for pain relief had lower death rates in the first week, but higher death rates by three months compared to those without blocks. Both groups had very high mortality rates overall, reflecting the frailty of elderly patients managed without surgery for hip fractures.

articles.title: Increased risk of early failure of multiply revised total hip arthroplasty.
articles.authors: D'Apollonio TM, Hopman MLT, Sullivan T, Abrahams JM, Sheth NP, Solomon LB, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing aseptic revision total hip arthroplasty
articles.sample_size: 838 aseptic revision hip replacements (710 patients): 598 first revisions, 155 second revisions, 85 third and beyond revisions
articles.outcomes: Re-revision rate and implant survivorship at two years; cumulative incidence of re-revision by revision number; risk factors for early failure
articles.take_home: Hips that have been revised multiple times have higher failure rates in the first two years after surgery, but the number of previous revisions alone does not independently increase re-revision risk when other factors are accounted for. Hip instability is the most common reason for early failure across all revision groups.

articles.title: Index Procedure Length of Stay and Achievement of Patient Acceptable Symptom State Predict Outcomes of Contralateral Total Hip Arthroplasty Within 1-Year.
articles.authors: Khan ST, Emara A, Zhang C, Jevnikar BE, Elmenawi K, Deren ME, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective analysis of prospective registry data
articles.population: Patients who underwent staged bilateral primary total hip arthroplasty within one year
articles.outcomes: Discharge disposition, prolonged length of stay (≥3 days), 90-day readmission, one-year reoperation, and Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score measures
articles.take_home: Patients experienced worse symptom improvement and more complications after their second hip replacement compared to their first. Not achieving good symptom relief after the first operation strongly predicted poor results after the second operation.

articles.title: A Comparative Study of Fixed-Bearing Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty for Spontaneous Osteonecrosis and Osteoarthritis of the Knee.
articles.authors: Liu P, Hou L, Chen Y, Jiang Y, Hu X, Li L, et al.
articles.population: Patients with spontaneous osteonecrosis of the knee or medial knee osteoarthritis undergoing fixed-bearing unicompartmental knee replacement
articles.sample_size: 50 patients (25 with osteonecrosis matched 1:1 with 25 with osteoarthritis)
articles.outcomes: Pain scores, knee function scores, range of motion, alignment, and postoperative complications at two years
articles.take_home: Fixed-bearing partial knee replacement works well for both spontaneous bone death and wear-related knee damage, with similar results at two years. Patients with bone death had more pain before surgery but improved more, though leg alignment correction was slightly less.

articles.title: Irritable Bowel Syndrome and Periprosthetic Joint Infection Risk Following Total Hip and Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Tan D, Anderson B, Kesick A, Parker J, Kapadia A, Ranson R, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database with propensity score matching
articles.population: Patients undergoing total hip arthroplasty or total knee arthroplasty, with and without irritable bowel syndrome
articles.sample_size: 19,102 patients with IBS history (7,144 hip, 11,958 knee) matched 1:1 with controls
articles.outcomes: Two-year periprosthetic joint infection rates and reoperation rates
articles.take_home: Irritable bowel syndrome alone did not increase infection risk after hip or knee replacement. However, IBS patients taking medications for their condition had a higher infection and reoperation risk after knee replacement, possibly because medication use reflects more severe disease.

articles.title: 10-Year Outcomes of Total Knee Arthroplasty for Fracture Compared to Osteoarthritis Indications.
articles.authors: Garcia D, Michael BR, Glenn ER, Agarwal AR, Suresh SJ, Thakkar SC
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using electronic health records
articles.population: Adults undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty for either fracture-indicated or osteoarthritis-indicated reasons
articles.sample_size: 1,062 patients in each cohort after propensity-score matching
articles.outcomes: 10-year all-cause revision, periprosthetic joint infection, aseptic loosening, periprosthetic fracture, and secondary fragility fracture
articles.take_home: Patients having knee replacement after a previous fracture had higher rates of infection and needing revision surgery at 10 years compared to those having replacement for osteoarthritis alone. These patients need extra care to prevent infection and closer monitoring after their operation.

articles.title: Field and Stream Recovery: Patient-Reported Return to Hunting and Fishing After Total Knee Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Lowden B, Burbelo A, Stone W, Clark T, Morgan C, Peluso R, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent total knee arthroplasty at a rural Appalachian academic medical centre between January 2019 and December 2024
articles.outcomes: Proportion of patients who resumed hunting and fishing, time to return, and willingness to recommend TKA
articles.take_home: Most patients who hunted or fished before their knee replacement were able to return to these activities within six months after surgery. Around 93% of patients said they would recommend knee replacement to others wanting to get back to hunting and fishing.

articles.title: Conversion of Patello-femoral Arthroplasty to Total Knee Arthroplasty: Survivorship, Function, and Predictors of Patellar Revision.
articles.authors: Carstens MF, Meissner N, Krych AJ, Pagnano MW, Taunton MJ, Lewallen DG, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent conversion of patello-femoral arthroplasty to total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Five-year survivorship free of revision (89.2%), five-year survivorship free of reoperation (83.9%), Knee Society Function score improvement from 59 to 80 at two years, patellar component revision rates based on pre-conversion patellar tilt
articles.take_home: Conversion of patello-femoral joint replacement to full knee replacement had good outcomes with 89% surviving without further revision at five years, and patients' function improved. Patients with significant tilting of the kneecap before surgery were more likely to need the patellar component revised during conversion.

articles.title: Preoperative Hip Abductor Muscle Strength Predicts Patient-Reported Functional Outcomes Following Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Huffman A, Burbelo A, Clark T, Annan C, Silcox DH 4th, Bullock M
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty for hip osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported functional outcomes at 12 months measured by Hip Disability and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score for Joint Replacement (HOOS-JR) and Veterans RAND 12-Item Health Survey (VR-12); achievement of minimal clinically important difference and patient-acceptable symptom state
articles.take_home: Patients with stronger hip abductor muscles before hip replacement surgery had better functional outcomes and quality of life scores at one year. The findings suggest that measuring hip muscle strength before surgery could help identify patients at risk of poorer recovery.

articles.title: Risk Factors for Readmission Following Same-Day Discharge in Primary Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Saba BV, Montague M, Markowitz M, Grossman E, Davidovitch R, Schwarzkopf R
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary elective total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Hospital readmission for orthopaedic-related reasons within 90 days
articles.take_home: Same-day discharge after hip replacement is safe with very low readmission rates (0.8%), but smoking and older age carry much higher readmission risk in this group than in patients staying overnight. Surgeons should pay extra attention to smoking status and age when deciding whether same-day discharge is appropriate for individual patients.

articles.title: Femoro-Tibial Size Mismatch Does Not Increase Polyethylene Wear in Fixed-Bearing Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Retrieval Analysis.
articles.authors: Mancino F, Sabharwal N, Greenaway M, Vlaskovsky P, Pabbruwe M, Jones CW
articles.population: Patients who had fixed-bearing total knee arthroplasty revisions
articles.outcomes: Polyethylene wear measured using modified Hood scoring system; implant survival; time in situ
articles.take_home: Size mismatch between the thigh bone and shin bone components did not lead to increased overall wear of the plastic liner in fixed-bearing knee replacements. Although slightly more wear was seen on the back surface when the thigh bone component was larger, this did not affect how long the implant lasted.

articles.title: Preoperative medial-compartment osteophytes do not adversely affect the outcome of lateral unicompartmental knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Schweizer C, Krug T, Abdulai S, Herre J, Aldinger PR, Merle C, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent lateral unicompartmental knee arthroplasty for isolated lateral-compartment osteoarthritis
articles.sample_size: 900 lateral unicompartmental knee arthroplasties in 830 patients
articles.outcomes: Reoperation-free survival, implant survivorship, medial-compartment disease progression requiring reoperation, and functional outcomes (Oxford Knee Score and UCLA Activity Score)
articles.take_home: The presence of bony growths in the inner part of the knee did not negatively affect outcomes in patients having partial knee replacement surgery for outer-compartment arthritis. Most patients did well after surgery regardless of whether they had these bony growths.

articles.title: Equivalent accuracy of image-based and imageless robotic platforms in achieving planned femoral rotation in primary total knee arthroplasty: A CT-based study.
articles.authors: Mancino F, Fernandez I, Parker DA, Fritsch BA
articles.population: Patients undergoing robotic-assisted total knee replacement for primary osteoarthritis
articles.outcomes: Accuracy of femoral rotation achieved during surgery, measured by comparing planned rotation to postoperative CT scans; patient-reported pain and outcomes
articles.take_home: Both image-based and imageless robotic systems achieved similar accuracy in positioning the femur during knee replacement, with rotational errors of about 1.2 to 1.3 degrees and no clinically meaningful differences between them. The image-based system showed slightly lower pain scores at 12 months, but this was the only notable difference in patient outcomes.

articles.title: Responsiveness and ceiling effects of Knee Injury and Osteoarthritis Outcome Score following anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: Evidence from the UK National Ligament Registry.
articles.authors: Searle HKC, Khatri C, Robinson J, O'Leary S, Hage W, Spalding T, et al.
articles.study_type: Secondary analysis of registry data, cohort study
articles.population: Patients undergoing anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Floor and ceiling effects, responsiveness and minimal important difference of four KOOS versions at baseline, 6 months, 1 year, 2 years and 5 years
articles.take_home: Most versions of the KOOS questionnaire show ceiling effects from 12 months after ACL reconstruction, meaning they cannot reliably distinguish between patients with better outcomes. KOOSglobal is less affected by this problem and may be more useful for tracking longer-term improvements.

articles.title: The rectus femoris tendon autograft in knee ligament reconstruction: Anatomy, biomechanics, clinical applications and results-A narrative review.
articles.authors: Glaab R, Ollivier M, Petersen W, Pineda T, Marot V, Quyen NQT, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing knee ligament reconstruction
articles.outcomes: Anatomical consistency, biomechanical properties including ultimate stress and elasticity, functional outcomes compared to hamstring tendon autografts, re-rupture rates
articles.take_home: The rectus femoris tendon shows promise as a graft source for knee ligament reconstruction with similar functional outcomes to hamstring tendons, but most evidence is short-term and low quality, so more high-quality long-term studies are needed to confirm whether it is truly better than existing options.

articles.title: Predicting ACL injury risk in athletes: A systematic review of machine learning-based models.
articles.authors: Bingol S, Hosseini E, Sahin BO, Tan C, Turan E, Baikoglu SB, et al.
articles.study_type: Systematic review of machine learning models
articles.population: Athletes
articles.sample_size: Ten studies included; individual studies ranged from 12 to larger cohorts
articles.outcomes: ACL injury risk prediction accuracy (ranging from 26% to 95%); Area Under Curve (AUC) ranging from 0.63 to 0.98 across different machine learning models
articles.take_home: Machine learning models show promise for predicting ACL injury risk in athletes, but most current studies have quality concerns and the highest accuracy rates come from small studies that may not work reliably in real-world settings. Better testing across different athlete populations is needed before these models can be used in clinical practice.

articles.title: Large language models as sources of patient information on robotic knee arthroplasty: a comparative evaluation.
articles.authors: Ciftci MU, Koluman AC, Aloglu Ciftci E, Cakmur BB, Ziroglu N
articles.study_type: Comparative evaluation of large language models
articles.population: Large language models (ChatGPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Flash, DeepSeek-V3) evaluated on robotic knee replacement patient questions
articles.sample_size: 20 frequently asked patient questions reviewed by 3 orthopaedic specialists
articles.outcomes: Reliability, usefulness, quality, and readability of AI-generated responses about robotic knee arthroplasty
articles.take_home: Gemini-2.5-Flash gave the most accurate and useful information about robotic knee replacement, whilst ChatGPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 were easier to read but less accurate. This suggests AI tools can help patients but need careful supervision from healthcare professionals.

articles.title: The impact of absolute change in tibiofemoral morphology on patient reported outcome measures post total knee arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Oon IH, Neeman T, Scarvell JM, Coltman CE, Smith PN, Spratford W, et al.
articles.study_type: Observational analysis of a randomised clinical trial
articles.population: Adults undergoing total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Patient reported outcome measures at six months including pain and satisfaction scales, Oxford Knee Score, Forgotten Joint Score, and Kujala Score; absolute change in knee alignment and morphology measurements
articles.take_home: The study found no clear relationship between how much the surgeon changed the knee's alignment and shape during surgery and how well patients felt six months later. Although the different measurements of alignment were linked together, these changes did not affect patient satisfaction or pain relief.

articles.title: Radiographic Factors Associated With Tibial Metaphyseal Sleeve Survivorship in Revision Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Matched Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Mazza PM, Colomb EL, Yarden JA, Moschetti WE
articles.population: Patients undergoing revision total knee replacement with tibial metaphyseal sleeves
articles.sample_size: 18 failed sleeves compared to 53 surviving sleeves (31 in matched analysis)
articles.outcomes: Implant survivorship; stem and sleeve fill ratios; medial baseplate support; aseptic failure rates
articles.take_home: Revision knee replacements using metaphyseal sleeves were more likely to survive long-term when the sleeve and stem filled the bone canal well and when the baseplate was properly supported. Poor fit of these components was associated with implant failure.

articles.title: A Comparative Analysis of Robotic-Assisted and Manual Techniques for Unicondylar Knee Arthroplasty Conversion to Total Knee Arthroplasty: Revision Component Use, Surgical Time, and Cost.
articles.authors: Aastroem KIM, Shah RP, Ferrara JAR, Whitmer LC, Geller JA, Kolodychuk N
articles.population: Patients undergoing conversion from unicondylar knee replacement to total knee replacement
articles.outcomes: Use of revision components (stems, cones, augments), polyethylene type, surgical time, implant cost, and postoperative complications
articles.take_home: Robotic-assisted surgery for converting a single-compartment knee replacement to a full knee replacement used fewer reinforcing stems, required less constrained plastic inserts, and cost less overall whilst taking less time than manual surgery. There was no difference in the need for cones or other augmentation between the two approaches.

articles.title: Periarticular Injection Alone Provides Comparable Early Recovery to Combined Adductor Canal and Infiltration between the Popliteal Artery and Capsule of the Knee Blocks Following Total Knee Arthroplasty: A Prospective Randomized Trial.
articles.authors: Schneider AM, Granger C, King J, Riegler V, Bartosiak KA, Bendich I, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total knee arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Visual analog scale pain scores, opioid consumption, Oxford Knee Scores, step counts, and patient satisfaction measured daily for two weeks after surgery
articles.take_home: Periarticular injection alone provided similar pain relief and recovery outcomes in the first two weeks after knee replacement compared to the more complex approach of combining regional nerve blocks with periarticular injection. This suggests that the simpler injection technique may be sufficient without adding regional blocks.

articles.title: Safety of Ketorolac in Primary Total Hip Arthroplasties: An Analysis of over 7,000 Cases.
articles.authors: Meissner N, Bonakdarhashemi M, Leung N, Duncan CM, Mabry TM, Taunton MJ, et al.
articles.population: Patients undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty
articles.outcomes: Acute kidney injury (AKI) according to KDIGO criteria, occurring in 3.4% of cases
articles.take_home: Ketorolac use during hip replacement surgery did not increase the risk of acute kidney injury, whether given by injection into the wound or intravenously. Patients with existing kidney disease, high blood pressure, obesity and those needing blood transfusions were at higher risk of kidney problems after surgery.

articles.title: Preoperative Methicillin-Resistant Staphylococcus aureus Colonization and Risk of Periprosthetic Joint Infection after Total Joint Arthroplasty: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
articles.authors: Javidmehr S, Javad Mortazavi SM, Rastegar M, Moradi M, Ebrahimian M, Siavashi B
articles.population: Patients undergoing total joint arthroplasty, classified by preoperative MRSA colonisation status
articles.sample_size: 15 studies, 318,487 patients (4,560 MRSA positive, 313,927 MRSA negative)
articles.outcomes: Periprosthetic joint infection and surgical site infection risk after total joint arthroplasty
articles.take_home: Patients who test positive for MRSA before joint replacement surgery remain at higher risk of infection even after decolonisation treatment, with more than double the risk of both deep joint infection and wound infection compared to MRSA-negative patients. Enhanced infection prevention strategies and closer monitoring may be needed for MRSA-positive patients.

articles.title: Diabetic Neuropathy Is Associated with Increased Orthopedic and Medical Complications After Total Hip Arthroplasty.
articles.authors: Kotzur T, VanderWeele BP, Barnes M, Jodoin Z, Moore C, Buttacavoli F
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national database
articles.population: Adults undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty, categorised into non-diabetic, diabetic without neuropathy, and diabetic with neuropathy groups
articles.sample_size: 193,483 patients (151,427 non-diabetic, 31,915 diabetic without neuropathy, 10,141 diabetic with neuropathy)
articles.outcomes: Two-year orthopaedic complications (joint infection, implant failure, fracture, revision surgery) and 90-day medical complications (pneumonia, wound disruption)
articles.take_home: Patients with diabetic neuropathy had higher rates of joint infection, implant problems, and need for revision surgery after hip replacement compared to diabetic patients without neuropathy. Doctors should assess for nerve damage from diabetes before hip replacement surgery to identify patients at higher risk of complications.

articles.title: Minimum Five-Year Results of Acetabular Revision Using Uncemented Monoblock Dual-Mobility Cups for Moderate to Severe Bone Loss.
articles.authors: Piercecchi A, Jacquet C, Rajillah O, Labattut L, Baulot E, Martz P
articles.population: Patients undergoing acetabular revision surgery with moderate to severe bone loss (Paprosky grade IIA or higher)
articles.outcomes: Aseptic acetabular loosening, acetabular re-revision, dislocation rate, functional outcomes (Harris Hip Score and Postel-Merle d'Aubigne score), radiographic assessment of hip centre of rotation restoration
articles.take_home: Uncemented monoblock dual-mobility cups showed good long-term stability in complex hip revision surgery with severe bone loss, with 93% of hips surviving without revision for loosening at ten years and low dislocation rates of 5%. Patients experienced significant improvement in hip function and pain scores.

articles.title: Increased tibial and meniscal slopes are risk factors for meniscal tears: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Zeng C, Borim FM, Thorne D, Lording T
articles.population: Patients with meniscal injuries compared to controls with intact menisci
articles.outcomes: Association between tibial slope, meniscal slope, meniscal bone angle and meniscal tears (medial, lateral, posterior root tears and ramp lesions)
articles.take_home: People with increased slope angles in their knee bones and menisci are at higher risk of meniscus tears. The study found the strongest link between increased slope angles and tears at the back of the meniscus, but more research is needed to understand how these measurements should guide patient care.

articles.title: Increased posterior tibial slope is associated with failure after anterior cruciate ligament primary repair.
articles.authors: Arras C, Mueller MM, Conner-Rilk S, Krishnan KR, Nash G, Monteleone TC, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective secondary analysis of prospectively collected cohort
articles.population: Patients aged 18 years or older who underwent arthroscopic anterior cruciate ligament primary repair for selected proximal ACL tears
articles.outcomes: Failure defined as objective knee laxity (side-to-side difference ≥3 mm, Lachman ≥2 or pivot-shift ≥2) and/or patient-reported symptomatic instability at 2-5 years follow-up. 24 patients (9.6%) met failure definition.
articles.take_home: Knees with a steeper backward slope of the tibia (particularly on the inner side) were more likely to fail after ACL repair surgery. This measurement could help surgeons and patients understand the risk of surgery not working when deciding whether to have this procedure.

articles.title: Condylar-constrained prostheses are associated with favourable implant survival following first-time aseptic revision knee arthroplasty: An analysis from the National Joint Registry.
articles.authors: Tyas B, Hewitt C, Deehan D, Baker P
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using national registry data
articles.population: Patients undergoing first-time aseptic revision knee replacement
articles.outcomes: 10-year cumulative incidence of re-revision; patient-reported outcome measures at 6 months; 90-day mortality and medical complications; length of stay
articles.take_home: Condylar-constrained knee prostheses had the best survival rates with only 9.2% needing further revision surgery within 10 years. Standard and unconstrained designs had higher re-revision rates, suggesting that using a more constrained design at revision surgery may give better long-term results.

articles.title: Revision rates are similar after surgical treatment of acute chondral and osteochondral injuries following patellar dislocation: A multicentre cohort study.
articles.authors: Hediger AM, Lustenberger T, Liechti EF, Hepp P, Samland M, Henkelmann R, et al.
articles.population: Patients who underwent surgical treatment for chondral and osteochondral injuries following patellar dislocation
articles.outcomes: Revision surgery rates, patient-reported outcome measures including Banff Patellofemoral Instability Instrument 2.0, EQ-5D, IKDC-2000 and Marx Activity Rating Scale
articles.take_home: Revision surgery rates were similar between patients with chondral injuries and osteochondral injuries after patellar dislocation, with about 11% of patients needing further surgery. Adding stabilising procedures at the time of initial surgery was associated with lower rates of needing revision surgery.

articles.title: An International Expert Consensus Statement Defining the Best Practices and Areas of Uncertainty Concerning the Use of Orthobiologics.
articles.authors: Kunze KN, Morgan JT, Gerhold C, Nishioka T, Piuzzi NS, Chahla J
articles.study_type: International expert consensus statement using Delphi methodology
articles.population: 24-member panel of international orthopaedic experts
articles.outcomes: Consensus statements on best practices for orthobiologics use, including platelet-rich plasma, bone marrow aspirate, amniotic derivatives, gene therapy and exosomes across various musculoskeletal conditions
articles.take_home: Experts reached broad agreement on when to use various orthobiologic treatments for conditions like osteoarthritis and tendon problems, but they identified significant gaps in knowledge about how to prepare these treatments, what doses to use, and how to ensure consistent quality across different clinics.

articles.title: Who Owns Arthroplasty Data?: Governance in the Era of Robotics, Registries, and Industry Partnerships.
articles.authors: Siddiqi A, Jacob PB, Yousuf KM
articles.take_home: This article discusses who controls and uses data from hip and knee replacement operations in the robotic and digital age, raising concerns that companies and registries may have too much control over surgical data whilst surgeons and patients have limited say in how their information is used.

articles.title: Harnessing the Biologic Power of Bacteriophages to Improve the Treatment of Periprosthetic Joint Infection: Barriers and Future Directions.
articles.authors: Abdelbary H, Malko S, Taha M, Crawley AM, Powell JN, Abedi AA, et al.
articles.population: Patients with periprosthetic joint infection
articles.outcomes: Potential of bacteriophage therapy as adjuvant treatment for periprosthetic joint infection; identification of barriers to clinical integration
articles.take_home: Bacteriophage therapy shows promise as an additional treatment for joint infections after replacement surgery, which currently fail in up to 30 per cent of cases. However, there is a gap between laboratory research and clinical use that needs to be addressed before this treatment can become standard practice.

articles.title: Integrated multidomain model for predicting meniscal injury in amateur athletes: Development of a personalized prevention algorithm.
articles.authors: Urresta FE, Penaherrera-Carrillo C, Castro AB
articles.population: Amateur athletes aged 15-50 years
articles.outcomes: Development of a multidomain predictive model for meniscal injury; derivation of a risk score (Meniscal Injury Risk Index) to stratify athletes into four risk categories
articles.take_home: Researchers developed a tool that combines information about knee structure, movement patterns, training load, health factors and symptoms to predict which amateur athletes are most likely to get a meniscal injury. The tool accurately identified at-risk athletes and could help guide personalised injury prevention strategies.

articles.title: Lexicon on the Pathomechanics of the Native Hip Joint at Risk for Arthritis.
articles.authors: Beaule PE, Beck M, Wagner M, Witt J, Grammatopoulos G, Zaltz I, et al.
articles.population: Patients with symptomatic, pre-arthritic hip disease
articles.outcomes: A structured lexicon defining morphological features and pathomechanical mechanisms of hip disease, including three principal wear modes (instability, impingement, mixed mechanisms) and classification of wear damage by tissue involvement
articles.take_home: Researchers and doctors have developed a standardised dictionary of terms to describe how hips develop arthritis through different mechanisms of wear and damage. This shared language should help improve communication between scientists and clinicians and lead to more consistent treatment approaches for people with hip problems that could lead to arthritis.
